newsitem.title: UK: UK's CBI calls for tightening, preferably fiscal.
newsitem.headline: UK's CBI calls for tightening, preferably fiscal.

text.p: Britain's economy is in need of either monetary or preferably fiscal tightening to check the build-up of inflationary pressures likely to follow the strength of domestic demand, the Confederation of British Industry said on WEdnesday.

"We believe that some tightening of the economy is necessary, either by interest rates or through the fiscal side," Andrew Buxton, chairman of the CBI's economic affairs committee told a news conference.
The CBI's chief economic adviser Kate Barker said that the CBI was still not convinced that the UK's public sector borrowing requirement was on the right track.
"This makes us favour fiscal rather than monetary tightening," she said.
Buxton said there was a danger that higher interest rates would strengthen sterling further, causing more damage to the export sector.
But he warned: "If we don't take some action, inflation will rise."
Barker, also one of Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke's independent advisers, declined to specify what sort of fiscal package was required.
